minutes.headline: Capital Planning heard IT, Fire and DPW requests, took no votes, and set a ranking process and Zoom meeting for Nov 13.
minutes.summary: The committee heard FY26 and out-year capital presentations from IT, the Fire Chief and the DPW director, with extensive questions on vehicles, grants and the stabilization fund. No substantive votes were taken. The chair outlined a process: a spreadsheet roll-up, individual ranking, then a final ranked list sent to the interim town manager by about the end of the calendar year, with meetings set for Nov 13 (hybrid/Zoom) and Dec 2.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment from the committee and the public at the start; none offered.
Closing public comment: none; no one on Zoom.

budget_items.topic: IT: Eagle House network equipment (Priority One, FY27)
budget_items.what_was_said: Eagle House network gear is end of life and unmanaged; request listed as a firewall, switches and access points package.

budget_items.topic: IT: network equipment replacement for other town buildings
budget_items.what_was_said: Minimum request meets the capital threshold; access points on a 5-year cycle, firewalls and switches closer to 7.
2022 equipment was funded by the grant, which can be applied for every 2 years; quotes are higher now than the original ask.
Town may offer a local share or ask for full funding; funds must be used within 12 months; the application is due in December.
Possible library server purchase, below the capital threshold.

budget_items.topic: Fire: FY26 Car 2 duty officer vehicle
budget_items.what_was_said: Replacement 4x4 pickup estimate, based on a nearby city's purchase.

budget_items.topic: Fire: eventual replacement of old car
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted the old vehicle may need replacing within years at a similar cost.
Estimate escalated 5% a year; chief may push it to FY28.

budget_items.topic: Fire: squad/rescue pumper replacement and AFG grant
budget_items.what_was_said: A federal grant needs an 80/20 match and fleet-age eligibility the town doesn't meet; chief suggests actual cost nearer a million.
The stabilization fund has been funded but never drawn for a large purchase; its intent was apparatus.
Bought for about 35,000 each and marked up for the placeholder.

budget_items.topic: Fire: vehicle costs over coming years
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted roughly three million in vehicles in four years, with an ambulance costing over half a million.
Line increased; buying five sets a year.
Nine portable radios coming with the ambulance via ARPA; more requested.
Chapter 90 funds used for paving and drainage; over seven hundred thousand spent this year.
Allotment is described as small and stagnant for about 12 years, with Fair Share money added.
Pavement management funded flat this year; the slide's higher figure was an estimated cost.
Price rose sharply from the quote two years ago; four sander trucks already on order.
MS4 permit calls for cleaning all catch basins yearly; staffing is the constraint.
Estimate is rough; cemetery sale of lots fund could pay but needs town meeting appropriation.
Members asked the town to look for cemetery grants using existing grant funds.
Rented a loader this year; recent repairs were made on the existing one.
Operating funds used for a tree removal contract; townwide survey requested.

budget_items.topic: DPW: salt shed construction and anti-icing
budget_items.what_was_said: Estimated construction cost, without a design.
Rebuild avoided a much higher replacement cost.
Average annual request is more than half of current annual capital spending.

decisions.decision: Committee to prioritize this year's requests and submit the order to the town manager by about the end of the calendar year.
The chair will roll the requests into a spreadsheet and share presentations in a Google share. Members will rank every project individually before the next meeting.
Next meeting set for Wednesday Nov 13 at about 7 pm by hybrid/Zoom; a December 2 in-person meeting is targeted, and Dec 16 is held as a backup.
Every member must rank every project, and the chair will try to get the list of uncompleted projects from the interim town manager.
Mean versus median for scoring is deferred to the next meeting.

what_happened.line: The Capital Planning Committee took no votes; it heard FY26 and out-year capital requests from IT, the Fire Chief and the DPW director.
The committee agreed to rank this year's requests and send the order to the town manager by about the end of the calendar year.
The chair will roll the requests into a spreadsheet, and every member will rank every project individually before the next meeting.
The next meeting is set for Wednesday Nov 13 by hybrid/Zoom, with a Dec 2 in-person meeting targeted and Dec 16 held as a backup.
Whether to score projects by mean or median was deferred to the next meeting.

why_it_matters: The ranked list sent to the town manager shapes which vehicles, equipment and building projects reach a future town meeting warrant, so residents may later be asked to vote on the items ranked highest.
Fire apparatus costs and the unused stabilization fund, which the committee noted was meant for apparatus, bear on whether big purchases are paid from savings or from borrowing and the tax levy.
watch_next: Nov 13 hybrid/Zoom meeting, where members' individual rankings and the mean-versus-median scoring question come up.
The final ranked list to the interim town manager, expected by about the end of the calendar year, after a Dec 2 meeting.
